answer: To curb Sybil attacks, an agent economy in lotus aquaculture authenticates peers using galvanic impedance spectroscopy across quartz and onyx gravel beds. Challenged nodes inject alternating currents to sample contact resistance; because simulating these stochastic mineral profiles is intractable, adversaries must deploy dedicated electrode hardware per entity. However, biofilm growth shifts baseline conductivity over time, causing false authentication rejections of honest nodes.
